newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-GRAHAM TAKES AUSTRALIAN TITLE AS WEBB FALTERS.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-GRAHAM TAKES AUSTRALIAN TITLE AS WEBB FALTERS.

text.p: Bogeys on the final two holes on Sunday cost Karrie Webb her first big win on home soil as Canada's Gail Graham came from five shots behind to win the Australian Ladies Masters by a stroke.
Webb, last year's U.S. LPGA Tour Rookie of the Year, had led by four shots overnight and pushed her lead to five before surrendering to Graham.
The Canadian carded a four-under-par 68 to finish on 15-under 273 and record only her second U.S. LPGA tournament success.

Webb finished one stroke back after a disappointing closing round of 73. She had earlier appeared to be in total control of the tournament, run jointly by the U.S. LPGA and Australian LPGA tours, before collapsing on the back nine.
The two players went to the 18th tee locked on 15 under. Webb could only reach the fringe of the green with her second short while Graham found the heart of the putting surface.
Webb then left her first putt 12 feet short and three-putted for a bogey five while Graham calmly got down with two putts..
World number one Laura Davies finished third on 275 after an aggressive closing round of 66.
